summary:
Burning Activity Calendar is a single-page web app that turns satellite active-fire detections into a year-by-week calendar for any area you choose.
The problem it addresses: MODIS and VIIRS can't be compared directly. VIIRS has a finer pixel and finds more small fires, so raw counts jump when VIIRS begins. 
Harmonization: For your area, it takes the ratio of VIIRS to MODIS detections over the fully overlapping years .The ratio is recomputed per area.
details:
What it does: A web app that turns satellite fire detections into one consistent year-by-week calendar for any area. MODIS (2000 onward) and VIIRS (2012 onward) can’t be compared directly, because VIIRS finds more small fires. The user picks an area. The app compares the two sensors over the years both cover (2013 onward) and rescales earlier MODIS counts to match VIIRS. The calendar can be coloured by how unusual each week is, and it also lists the busiest weeks of a normal year and the most unusual weeks on record.

Benefits:

  • Responders can see when fire seasons normally peak.
  • Land managers can tell whether a season is unusual.
  • Scientists get a record in which all years are comparable.
  • It needs no account or server, and it keeps data on the user’s device.

Impact: People who work with fire can tell real changes from changes of sensor. That supports earlier preparation, better use of resources and tracking of long-term shifts. It is free and light, so small agencies and students can use it.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript with the canvas, NASA FIRMS CSV files, Node.js with pptxgenjs for the slides, and Claude as an AI assistant. Any laptop or phone with a browser is enough.

Creativity: It shows when fires happen, not just where. It colours weeks by unusualness, recalculates the sensor ratio for each area, and shows raw against harmonized totals. It is a single file that anyone can host.

Factors considered: Sensor differences, overlap years, local variation, data quality, skewed counts, mobile use and privacy. Limits: the demo data is synthetic, one ratio per area ignores seasonal and land-cover differences, and the method hasn’t been validated against real FIRMS data.
